title: Add heterogeneous load tempering and request-fingerprint canary
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: production canaries today assume fairly homogeneous traffic slices which misses regressions that only surface under mixed-load cohorts (e.g., high-concurrency short-seq vs low-concurrency long-seq). This PR introduces a heterogeneous load tempering controller and a lightweight request-fingerprint layer so canary evaluators can (1) slice traffic by inferred execution footprint, (2) apply per-cohort probing/tempering policies, and (3) produce cohort-aware fingerprints for robust drift isolation.

Summary of changes (single-line checklist): - Implement tempering scheduler that can attenuate synthetic probe rates per-cohort; - Add request fingerprint extractor (sequence-length, kv-cache-hit, concurrency-hint) and scoring; - Extend canary evaluator to accept cohort-weighted signals and produce per-cohort regression alerts; - Add rollout policy that soft-fails traffic to primary model only after sustained cross-cohort consensus; - Add unit/integration tests and e2e canary harness job; - Update docs and runbook excerpt.

Design notes: The tempering scheduler runs as a low-impact control loop inside the perf-canary orchestrator. It surfaces a small token-bucket shaped budget per cohort and dynamically reduces synthetic probe injection when cohort-level variance increases, preventing probes from amplifying instabilities. The request-fingerprint is intentionally minimal (no heavy sampling): it hashes a tuple {sequence_length_bucket, kv_cache_presence, payload_signature_prefix, inferred_concurrency_class} into a 64-bit fingerprint used for grouping. Canary evaluator changes include an additional aggregation axis (cohort_id) and a consensus gate that requires at least two cohorts to exceed regression thresholds before initiating an automated rollback.

Rollout plan: feature branch -> internal canary (10% traffic, synthetic probes enabled) -> monitor for 24h with new cohort dashboards -> escalate to 50% if stable -> merge and ship. Automatic soft-fallback will divert synthetic probes to a spectator pool if stability score < 0.7.

Commits: - 4f9a2d3: initial tempering scheduler core loop and interfaces; - 7b2f1ac: fingerprint extractor and unit tests; - d2c5e01: add cohort-aware aggregation in evaluator; - 8a1bff7: e2e harness job and CI pipeline steps; - c3e4a0b: docs + runbook.

Changed files (high level): - perf-canary/orchestrator/tempering.go (new) - perf-canary/evaluator/cohort_aggregator.go (modified) - perf-canary/evaluator/cohort_aggregator_test.go (new) - perf-canary/ingress/fingerprint.go (new) - perf-canary/harness/e2e_tempering.yml (new CI job) - docs/canary/heterogeneous-tempering.md (new) - scripts/bench/probe_simulator.py (updated sample traffic shapes)

Small illustrative snippet (tempering config schema): "tempering_rate: {base_probe_rps: 0.5, max_burst: 5, quiesce_threshold: 0.25, cohort_weights: {short_seq: 0.4, long_seq: 0.6}}"

Tests & CI: added 45 unit tests and a lightweight integration scenario that runs the probe simulator against a local evaluator instance. CI shows an initial flaky lint failure on gofmt in orch package (fixed in 7b2f1ac). The full e2e job was added to the perf-check pipeline and passed on the final run.

Review conversation (timeline condensed): - Evan Chen (review): "Nice approach; two asks: 1) Please ensure fingerprint entropy avoids correlating with user IDs; 2) Add a fallback path if fingerprint extraction fails under malformed payloads." - Priya (author): "Addressed: salt the prefix hash with a server-side stable key and fall back to 'unknown' cohort when parsing fails — updated tests." - Lars Becker (review): "Can we instrument the tempering decisions for 1w retention? Need this for postmortems." - Priya: "Added telemetry + retention flag (configurable) in docs; default 72h." - Aisha Kumar (approval): "Approved pending small docs clarifications."

Operational considerations: telemetry added: canary.cohort.{ingress_rate,probe_rate,variance,stability_score,tempering_action}. Retention is configurable per-deployment. The runbook includes steps to disable cohort slicing if noisy signals are observed and a quick CLI flag to revert to legacy single-slice canary.

Related work and references: builds on prior probe-reservoir work (ENG-1871) and the adaptive-probe-rescheduler (ENG-1989). Linear tickets linked above. SUP-712 triggered a hotfix during a customer incident where mixed traffic masked a regression; this PR aims to prevent similar misses.

Release notes: Added heterogeneous load tempering controller and request-fingerprint based cohorting for canary evaluations. This enables cohort-aware regression detection and reduces false negatives when regressions only affect specific workload patterns.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main after approvals and green CI.

Follow-ups (non-blocking): - Add privacy review for fingerprinting step (P0 for regulated customers) - Add SDK-level hooks to surface cohort annotations in telemetry - Run a 72h internal soak with three production-like workload mixes.

release_notes: Adds heterogeneous cohort-based tempering scheduler and request fingerprinting to improve canary sensitivity for mixed-workload regressions. New metrics and a runbook are included.
runbook_excerpt: If cohort instability observed: 1) disable cohort slicing (cli flag: --canary-cohorting=false), 2) rerun baseline probes at reduced rate, 3) escalate if stability_score < 0.5 across multiple cohorts.
notes_for_security_review: Fingerprinting uses non-identifying buckets and a server-side salt; PHI/PII not stored. Security review recommended before enabling long-term retention for regulated customers.
